definitions.explanation: White cotton gloves with a knitted texture, commonly used for manual labor and gardening.

examples.japanese: {草|くさ}むしりをするので{軍手|ぐんて}をはめた。
examples.english: I put on work gloves to pull weeds.

examples.japanese: {軍手|ぐんて}なしで{作業|さぎょう}すると{手|て}が{汚|よご}れる。
examples.english: If you work without gloves, your hands will get dirty.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しの{時|とき}は{軍手|ぐんて}があると{便利|べんり}だ。
examples.english: Work gloves are handy when moving house.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
{軍手|ぐんて} originally meant "military gloves" ({軍|ぐん} = military + {手|て} = hand), as they were once standard issue for the Japanese military. Now they are everyday work gloves.

USAGE:
{軍手|ぐんて} are inexpensive, disposable cotton gloves sold in packs. Common uses include:
・{庭仕事|にわしごと} (gardening)
・{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}し (moving)
・{掃除|そうじ} (cleaning)
・DIY{作業|さぎょう} (DIY work)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{軍手|ぐんて}をはめる (to put on work gloves)
・{軍手|ぐんて}を{外|はず}す (to take off work gloves)

COUNTER: {双|そう} or {組|くみ} (for pairs)
